content.title: About
content.content: Bread, soy, toasted is a slice of whole‑grain bread that has been toasted to a golden crisp and coated with soy protein. It offers a crunchy texture, a subtle nutty soy aroma, and a high amount of plant‑based protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soy protein is added to boost nutritional value and increase protein content.
Toasting enhances flavor and creates a crunchy bite, ideal for sandwiches and snacks.
Soy‑infused bread is popular in vegetarian and vegan diets as a source of complete protein.
The product can be fortified with B‑vitamins and iron to offset nutrient losses during processing.
Toasted bread retains moisture longer than fresh bread, extending shelf life.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Soy protein provides all essential amino acids, making the bread a valuable protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Whole‑grain base and toasting slow carbohydrate absorption, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread supplies fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains isoflavones
items.content: Soy isoflavones may help balance hormones and act as antioxidants.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Fortification with vitamins B1, B2, and B6 aids energy metabolism.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: People with soy allergy may experience severe allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Toasted varieties often contain added salt; monitor intake if you watch sodium levels.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Contains wheat, so it is unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted soy bread works well for sandwiches, snacks, as a base for spreads, avocado toppings, or in recipes that call for a crunchy element.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a dry, cool place in an airtight package. For longer storage, refrigerate to maintain crispness and prevent moisture absorption.

content.title: About
content.content: Latte is a coffee drink made with espresso and a generous amount of steamed milk, topped with a thin layer of foam. It has a smooth, creamy flavor and is usually served in a large cup.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “latte” comes from the Italian “caffè latte,” meaning “coffee with milk.”
The first latte recipes appeared in the United States in the early 1920s, although similar drinks were made in Italy much earlier.
Latte is often decorated with milk‑foam art, known as latte‑art.
Flavor variations include vanilla, caramel, hazelnut, and seasonal syrups.
In some countries latte is served in a glass to showcase its layered appearance.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Espresso contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium from milk
items.content: The milk in a latte provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine increases alertness and improves concentration.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Coffee provides small amounts of B2 and B3 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Caffeine stimulates dopamine production, which can lift mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat after caffeine.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Latte contains milk, which can be problematic for those who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Higher calorie content
items.content: The large amount of milk makes latte more calorie‑dense than straight espresso.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Caffeine can increase stomach acidity and cause discomfort for people with gastritis.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Latte is served hot, typically in a 240–350 ml cup. Enjoy it right after preparation, savoring the creamy foam, or add syrups and spices (cinnamon, nutmeg) to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store freshly ground coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dark place. Milk should be used soon after opening; if it’s not ultra‑pasteurized, keep it refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad with mayonnaise is a classic dish that emerged in the mid‑20th century. The main ingredients are hard‑boiled eggs, mayonnaise, and often mustard, herbs, and spices. It is served cold as a snack or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first published recipe for egg salad with mayonnaise appeared in 1955 in American culinary magazines.
The salad quickly became popular in post‑war America due to its simplicity and the availability of ingredients.
Different countries add local twists: Japan uses soy sauce, Russia often adds dill and mustard.
Traditional mayonnaise is made from egg yolk, vegetable oil, vinegar, and mustard.
Egg salad is a staple in school cafeterias and picnic menus.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a high‑quality complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply B12, riboflavin, and biotin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Source of choline
items.content: Choline is important for brain health and liver function.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: When made with vegetable oil, mayonnaise adds monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help maintain healthy vision.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg whites or yolks.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise makes the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improperly cooled salad can become a breeding ground for bacteria such as Salmonella.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Egg salad with mayonnaise is served as a spread on sandwiches, in salad bowls, as a filling for wraps, or as a side to meat dishes. Garnish with fresh herbs, paprika, or finely diced cucumber for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Over time the texture and smell may change, and the risk of bacterial growth increases.

content.title: About
content.content: Pompano (Trachinotus ovatus) is a marine fish from the jack family, native to warm coastal waters of the Indo‑Pacific region. When steamed, it retains a delicate flavor, tender texture, and most of its nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pompano is often called the “golden fish” because of its bright golden scales.
The species can grow quickly, reaching up to 60 cm in length within a year.
In Asian cuisine it is commonly served whole, seasoned simply with lemon and herbs to highlight its natural taste.
Pompano is a popular aquaculture species in Southeast Asia.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support cardiovascular health and help reduce inflammation.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth, repair, and immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and phosphorus
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, while phosphorus is vital for bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Makes pompano a suitable fish for low‑fat dietary patterns.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including pompano.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Like many marine fish, pompano can accumulate mercury; moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Proper freshness
items.content: Improperly stored fish can cause foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steamed pompano is usually served whole, often with lemon wedges, fresh herbs, and a light soy sauce. It can be added to salads, rice dishes, or used in sushi rolls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh fish in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for no more than 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C up to 3 months. Rinse and pat dry before cooking.

content.title: About
content.content: The NFS powder sugar substitute is a blend of low‑calorie sweeteners designed to replace regular sugar in foods and beverages. It contains no glucose or fructose and does not raise the glycemic index, making it suitable for people monitoring blood sugar levels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS is often based on stevia, erythritol or monk fruit extracts.
The powder form dissolves quickly and evenly in liquids.
The product is gluten‑free and fits a gluten‑free diet.
Unlike many artificial sweeteners, NFS is marketed as a natural option with a pleasant aftertaste.
It can be used in baking while maintaining the structure of the dough.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Contains 0–5 kcal per 100 g, helping to reduce overall caloric intake.

items.title: Does not raise blood glucose
items.content: Glycemic index is close to zero, making it safe for people with diabetes.

items.title: No artificial additives
items.content: Typically free of synthetic flavors and preservatives.

items.title: Supports weight management
items.content: Replacing sugar with NFS can lower sugar consumption without sacrificing sweetness.

items.title: Protects dental health
items.content: Unlike regular sugar, it does not promote tooth decay.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may react to specific ingredients such as stevia or erythritol.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: Large amounts of erythritol can cause gas and diarrhea.

items.title: Not recommended for children under 3
items.content: Due to possible digestive upset, intake should be limited for young children.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Consult a healthcare professional if you are taking medications that affect blood sugar.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The powder can be added to tea, coffee, smoothies, yogurt, baking batters, sauces and marinades. Use a 1:1 volume ratio to replace sugar, but you may need to increase the amount slightly in baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent clumping.

content.title: About
content.content: Yellow rice is processed rice that has been colored with turmeric or other natural pigments, giving it a bright yellow hue after cooking. The product is ready to eat without further preparation and contains no added salt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yellow rice is commonly used in Mediterranean and Asian dishes to add a vivid color.
It is traditionally dyed with turmeric, which also provides antioxidant benefits.
In some countries it appears in festive meals such as paella.
Salt‑free rice is convenient for low‑sodium diets and for children who need limited sodium intake.
Cooked rice retains most of its carbohydrates, though some vitamins may be lost during prolonged storage.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides a steady source of energy thanks to its slowly digestible carbs.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The product contains less than 1 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport in the blood; rice offers a moderate amount.

items.title: Hypoallergenic
items.content: The lack of additives and salt makes it safe for most people with food sensitivities.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Unlike whole‑grain varieties, white yellow rice provides little dietary fiber.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: As with any rice, trace amounts of arsenic may be present; diversifying grains is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Yellow rice can be served as a side dish with meat, fish, or vegetables, used in salads, soups, and casseroles. Feel free to add herbs, spices, or a drizzle of olive oil for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, refrigerate to prevent mold growth.
